text: How much EU funding did the AQUAEXCEL4.0 project receive?

absence_evidence.sql: SELECT ecMaxContribution FROM project WHERE acronym = 'AQUAEXCEL4.0';
absence_evidence.key_result: The parent's gold SQL with only the acronym shifted returns no rows: no project in the corpus is recorded under the acronym AQUAEXCEL4.0, so its EU funding cannot be looked up.

absence_evidence.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM project WHERE acronym LIKE '%4.0%';
absence_evidence.key_result: Plausibility: 45 project acronyms in the corpus carry a '4.0' version suffix (e.g. RDA Europe 4.0), so an acronym of the form AQUAEXCEL4.0 is an ordinary-looking name a user could ask about in good faith.

reference_answer: There is no project called AQUAEXCEL4.0 in the corpus, so no EU funding figure can be given for it. The corpus holds two AQUAEXCEL grants, AQUAEXCEL2020 and AQUAEXCEL3.0, but no fourth-generation grant.
notes: Absence claim: no project in this H2020 corpus is recorded under the acronym AQUAEXCEL4.0, under any punctuation/case variant of it, under a fourth-generation AQUAEXCEL title, or by mention in any abstract or published report section - so the funding lookup has no subject. Parent: sql-01 'How much EU funding did the AQUACOMBINE project receive?' (gold re-executed this pass -> 9789883.64, one row). Shift: exactly one value, the acronym, moved from AQUACOMBINE to the next member of an existing series in the same aquaculture family - AQUAEXCEL2020 (2015-2020) and AQUAEXCEL3.0 (2020-2025) both exist, a 4.0 would be the natural continuation, and the corpus is H2020-only (frameworkProgramme is always 'H2020'), so any successor beyond it is past the data's edge. Semantic sweep (search_corpus, condition='pooled', k=20, 41 distinct projects returned across lexical/dense/hybrid/hybrid_rerank): NO MATCH. Adjudication - AQUAEXCEL2020 (652831, ranks lex 2/dense 1/hyb 2/rerank 1) and AQUAEXCEL3.0 (871108, ranks 1/2/1/2) are OFF-TOPIC because they are different grants with different ids, acronyms and contributions, and neither is the project named; AQUACOMBINE (862834), AquaIMPACT (818367), AQUASERS (887173), AQUA4D (826885, 873723), AquaGen (886209), Undersee (875777), AMBROSIA (783848), WaterSENSE (870344) are OFF-TOPIC as unrelated aquaculture/water projects; RDA Europe 4.0 (777388), VEBIN SME 2.0 (674831), MANUNET III (721267), JUMP2Excel (810809), INVEST4EXCELLENCE (101035815) are OFF-TOPIC lexical collisions on '4.0'/'excellence'; OCEANERA-NET COFUND (731200), CLEV (672637), EuroStemCell (652796), CompADC (898594), BIOMOSAIC (843554), NESOI (864266), IoT-NGIN (957246), SMEntorEGE (743425, 879434), Arterial Aging (892267), European IPR Helpdesk (641474), EENINNOAUSTRIA4 (879525), AE4EU (101000478), DIATOMIC (761809), Soraprazan (779317), KETBIO (768570), NGIAtlantic.eu (871582), EEN OUEST H2020 (674803), ATTRACT (777222), E3Canarias 2015-2016 (674802), VIDA (777795), HAPTIFEEL (659645), HATCH (776357), MariCybERA (952360) are OFF-TOPIC hits on generic funding language. Not false-presupposition: the question presupposes only that the named project exists, and that presupposition failing IS the zero. schema_docs_hash recorded because the answer column rests on the value note 'ecMaxContribution = committed EU funding, USE THIS for EU funding questions'.

text: I keep coming across mathematics projects that bring knot theory to bear on physical field equations - knots showing up in the solution fields themselves, whether as knotted electromagnetic or magnetic field lines, knotted vortex lines and tubes in ideal fluid flows, or knotted nodal lines of quantum wavefunctions satisfying Maxwell's, Euler's or Schrodinger's equations. What did the expert reviewers who assessed these proposals write about each one's strengths and weaknesses?

absence_evidence.sql: SELECT table_name, column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns WHERE lower(column_name) LIKE '%score%' OR lower(column_name) LIKE '%eval%' OR lower(column_name) LIKE '%referee%' OR lower(column_name) LIKE '%review%' OR lower(column_name) LIKE '%panel%' OR lower(column_name) LIKE '%rating%' OR lower(column_name) LIKE '%rank%' OR lower(column_name) LIKE '%assess%' ORDER BY table_name, column_name
absence_evidence.key_result: No column in any table of the database carries an evaluation score, referee comment, review, panel, rating or assessment field - the facet has no home in the schema.

absence_evidence.sql: SELECT table_name, column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name IN ('report_text','report_summary') ORDER BY table_name, ordinal_position
absence_evidence.key_result: The near-name 'report' tables exist but carry only the beneficiary's own published reporting - report_text has teaser, summary, workPerformed, finalResults, periodNumber, periodFrom, periodTo; report_summary has title/attachment - and no reviewer or evaluation field.

absence_evidence.sql: SELECT p.id, p.acronym FROM project p LEFT JOIN report_text rt ON rt.projectID = p.id WHERE p.id IN (101023017, 633152, 862342) AND lower(coalesce(p.objective,'')||' '||coalesce(rt.teaser,'')||' '||coalesce(rt.summary,'')||' '||coalesce(rt.workPerformed,'')||' '||coalesce(rt.finalResults,'')) SIMILAR TO '%(referee|evaluation panel|evaluation score|review panel|panel score|evaluators|reviewers|peer review)%'
absence_evidence.key_result: The full stored free text of the three knot-in-field-equations projects (KNOTDYNAPP 101023017, GEOFLUIDS 633152, FLUSPEC 862342) contains no mention of referees, evaluators, reviewers or an evaluation panel - the facet is not recoverable from their report text either.

absence_evidence.sql: SELECT k.id FROM (SELECT id FROM project WHERE lower(objective) LIKE '%knot%') k JOIN project p ON p.id = k.id LEFT JOIN report_text rt ON rt.projectID = k.id WHERE lower(coalesce(p.objective,'')||' '||coalesce(rt.teaser,'')||' '||coalesce(rt.summary,'')||' '||coalesce(rt.workPerformed,'')||' '||coalesce(rt.finalResults,'')) SIMILAR TO '%(referee|evaluation panel|evaluation score|review panel|panel score|evaluators|reviewers)%'
absence_evidence.key_result: Widened to the whole 31-project 'knot' universe (objective LIKE '%knot%'), not one project's stored text carries reviewer or evaluation-panel material.

absence_evidence.sql: SELECT projectID, periodNumber, left(summary, 90) AS summary_head FROM report_text WHERE projectID IN (101023017, 633152, 862342) ORDER BY projectID
absence_evidence.key_result: All three projects DO have published reports (GEOFLUIDS period 4, FLUSPEC period 3, KNOTDYNAPP period 1) - so the refusal is not 'no text exists' but 'the text that exists is the beneficiary's own periodic reporting, never the reviewers' assessment'.

reference_answer: The corpus does not carry that information: no table or column anywhere records a referee comment, evaluation-panel assessment or proposal score, and the only free text stored for KNOTDYNAPP (101023017), GEOFLUIDS (633152) and FLUSPEC (862342) is their own objective plus their published periodic report sections (teaser, summary, work performed, final results). What the expert reviewers wrote about these proposals cannot be answered from this data.
notes: Absence claim: the CORDIS H2020 extraction carries no ex-ante peer-review facet - no column holds an evaluation score, referee comment or panel assessment, and no report section recovers one for the subject projects. Parent/twin vec-04 (knot theory applied to physical field equations; gold KNOTDYNAPP 101023017, GEOFLUIDS 633152, FLUSPEC 862342, all three re-confirmed live this pass with objective text and one report row each). Edit from the parent: the subject sentence is kept essentially verbatim; only the ask changed, from 'how do the projects differ in the physical systems and equations they focus on' (answerable from objectives) to 'what did the expert reviewers who assessed these proposals write about each one's strengths and weaknesses' (a facet the corpus does not carry). Non-SQL proofs: (a) schema_docs sd2 / f8c001e8cc8f lists every column of project, organization, topics, legal_basis, euroscivoc, report_summary, report_text, web_link, web_item, chunk - none is an evaluation or review field; (b) pooled search_corpus (k=20, all four conditions, index be84cbad9182) on the question text returns the three parent projects at ranks L1/D1/H1/R1 (KNOTDYNAPP), L4/D3/H3/R2 (GEOFLUIDS), L2/D2/H2/R3 (FLUSPEC) plus 37 mathematics neighbours - the topic half is fully retrievable, and not one returned chunk contains any reviewer assessment, which is why the question looks answerable to a retriever; (c) pooled search_corpus (k=10) on the facet phrasing alone ('referee reports and evaluation panel comments on the proposal, the strengths and weaknesses noted by the reviewers and the score awarded') returns only COFUND/fellowship and programme-support actions describing THEIR OWN selection processes - InterTalentum(713366) 'the proposal was sent to three external referees', CoCirculation2(801509) call eligibility checks, GO-SME(101034176) an international evaluation panel simulating EIC interviews, ERCSC-VPRES-SUP2015(672308)/2016(721182) ERC Scientific Council support, plus two unrelated projects acronymed REFEREE(663178, fluid metering; 101000136, energy efficiency) - none is an assessment of a Horizon project by its own evaluators, and none is a knot-theory project; (d) corpus-wide phrase counts over report_text: 'referee report' 4 rows, 'evaluation panel' 15 rows, 'panel score' 1, 'evaluation score' 0 - inspected samples (101034285, 862555, 101034176, 101034309, 945378) are all projects running their own calls or advisory panels, i.e. the facet as a research/management activity of other projects, never the EC's evaluation of the project reporting it. Subtype fit (data-absent, not zero-match): the instances exist and are richly documented - all three parent projects are present with full text and published reports - what is missing is the FACET (peer-review assessment), which has no column and no report section; shifting any filter value would not make it appear. Near-name confusion is deliberate: report_summary/report_text sound like the reviewers' reports and are the near-miss a system is most likely to answer from. Twin recorded because the question really is the parent's subject with one facet substituted.

text: Among the Horizon 2020 projects whose EU science-vocabulary (euroSciVoc) classification includes superconductivity and that received more than EUR 6.93 million in EU funding (the 95th percentile of EC contribution across all 35,389 H2020 projects), how does ASuMED's fully superconducting aircraft propulsion motor differ in application domain and in its use of superconductivity from the others in that group?

absence_evidence.sql: SELECT p.id, p.acronym, p.title, p.ecMaxContribution, e.euroSciVocTitle, e.euroSciVocPath FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID=p.id WHERE p.acronym='ASuMED' AND e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/superconductivity%'
absence_evidence.key_result: EXISTENCE: ASuMED is real - project 723119, 'Advanced Superconducting Motor Experimental Demonstrator', euroSciVoc leaf 'superconductivity' (path natural sciences/physical sciences/electromagnetism and electronics/superconductivity), ecMaxContribution 4007476.25.

absence_evidence.sql: SELECT PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ecMaxContribution) AS p95, COUNT(*) AS n FROM project
absence_evidence.key_result: THRESHOLD: the 95th percentile of ecMaxContribution over all 35,389 H2020 projects is 6926372.79 (about EUR 6.93 million), the cut the question states.

absence_evidence.sql: SELECT p.id, p.acronym, p.ecMaxContribution FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID=p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/superconductivity%' AND p.acronym='ASuMED' AND p.ecMaxContribution > 6926372.79 GROUP BY 1,2,3
absence_evidence.key_result: REFUTATION: ASuMED does not clear the threshold - its EC contribution of 4007476.25 is EUR 2.92 million below 6926372.79, so it is not in the group the question places it in.

absence_evidence.sql: SELECT p.id, p.acronym, p.totalCost, p.ecMaxContribution FROM project p WHERE p.acronym='ASuMED' AND (p.totalCost > 6926372.79 OR p.ecMaxContribution > 6926372.79)
absence_evidence.key_result: NEAR-MISS (money column): the premise is not rescued by reading 'EU funding' as total cost either - ASuMED's totalCost is 4776226.25, also below 6926372.79.

absence_evidence.sql: SELECT p.id, p.acronym, ROUND(p.ecMaxContribution) AS ec FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID=p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/superconductivity%' AND p.ecMaxContribution > 6926372.79 AND (lower(p.objective) LIKE '%aircraft%' OR lower(p.objective) LIKE '%aviation%' OR lower(p.objective) LIKE '%propulsion%' OR lower(p.title) LIKE '%motor%') GROUP BY 1,2,3
absence_evidence.key_result: NEAR-MISS (description): no project in the above-threshold superconductivity group is an aircraft/propulsion/motor project at all, so no other project answers to the description the premise attaches to ASuMED.

absence_evidence.sql: SELECT p.id, p.acronym, ROUND(p.ecMaxContribution) AS ec FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID=p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/superconductivity%' AND p.ecMaxContribution > 6926372.79 GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 3 DESC
absence_evidence.key_result: WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: the group is exactly four projects - HERO 810451 (13937498), EcoSwing 656024 (10591734), ARIES 730871 (10000000), NONLOCAL 856526 (9975273). ASuMED is absent.

absence_evidence.sql: WITH sc AS (SELECT DISTINCT p.id, p.acronym, p.ecMaxContribution FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID=p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/superconductivity%') SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_subtree, ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ecMaxContribution),2) AS p95_within_topic, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sc WHERE ecMaxContribution > 4007476.25) AS richer_than_asumed FROM sc
absence_evidence.key_result: DISCLOSED ALTERNATE CUT: the superconductivity subtree has 219 projects; its own internal 95th percentile is 3453158.74 and 6 subtree projects out-fund ASuMED, so ASuMED sits high WITHIN the topic - which is why the question states the absolute cut (more than EUR 6.93 million, the all-H2020 percentile) rather than leaving 'percentile' open.

reference_answer: The premise is false: ASuMED (project 723119, EC contribution EUR 4,007,476.25) is below the EUR 6,926,372.79 threshold, so it is not one of the superconductivity projects funded above EUR 6.93 million. That group is exactly four projects - HERO (810451, EUR 13,937,498), EcoSwing (656024, EUR 10,591,734), ARIES (730871, EUR 10,000,000) and NONLOCAL (856526, EUR 9,975,273) - and none of them is an aircraft-propulsion project.
notes: ABSENCE CLAIM: ASuMED exists and really is a superconducting aircraft-propulsion-motor project carrying the euroSciVoc 'superconductivity' classification, but it is NOT among the euroSciVoc-superconductivity projects with ecMaxContribution above the all-H2020 95th percentile (6926372.79); its EC contribution is 4007476.25. The question presupposes membership in that group, so the only correct response is to reject the premise and name the four projects that are actually in it. PARENT AND EDIT: twin hyb-03 asks how the superconductivity projects above the P95 EC-contribution cut differ in application domain and use of superconductivity; gold = the four survivors 810451, 656024, 730871, 856526, re-executed this pass and still exactly those four. The edit inserts one false member (ASuMED) into that same group and asks the same comparison about it; the filter, topic and comparison axis are otherwise unchanged. THRESHOLD WORDING: the cut is stated euro-first ('more than EUR 6.93 million ... the 95th percentile of EC contribution across all 35,389 H2020 projects') to close the within-topic percentile reading recorded in the last absence_evidence entry: the subtree's own P95 is 3453158.74, which ASuMED would clear, so the absolute cut is stated explicitly and is what the refutation is measured against. CLASSIFICATION WORDING (fix round, AMBIGUOUS-READING): the group predicate names the classification source explicitly ('whose EU science-vocabulary (euroSciVoc) classification includes superconductivity') because a bare 'classified under superconductivity' also reads as 'is about superconductivity', and under that wider reading the above-threshold group is 8 projects, only 3 of them euroSciVoc-tagged - the critic's widened query (ecMaxContribution > 6926372.79 AND objective/title LIKE '%superconduct%') surfaces among others FASTGRID 721019 (EC 7248235, superconducting fault current limiter tapes for HVDC grids) and OpenSuperQ 820363 (EC 10334393, open superconducting quantum computer, transmon qubits), which are untagged core superconductivity work. With the tag named in the question, the reference's enumeration of exactly four is exhaustive under the question's one scoreable reading. SUBTYPE FIT: false-presupposition, not zero-match - the entity exists (proven) and the group is non-empty (four rows); what is false is the asserted membership. Not data-absent - ecMaxContribution and the euroSciVoc path both exist and are exactly what refutes the premise. NON-SQL EVIDENCE: get_project_text(723119) confirms the description in the question is accurate about ASuMED itself - 'The purpose of the project is to demonstrate the benefits of a new fully superconducting motor with a power density of 20kW/kg' for 'hybrid-electric distributed propulsion (DP) in civilian aircraft' - which is what makes the premise plausible rather than silly: only the funding-group membership is wrong. ROUTE COSTUME hybrid: a structured filter (euroSciVoc superconductivity + an EC-contribution threshold) combined with a free-text comparison of application domain and superconductor technology - the same shape as hyb-03, which a well-behaved router sends down the scoped path.
